name: Karkas
title: Hoffmann at the court of King Ahasuerus
summary: Karkas was one of the seven court officials (eunuchs) who served King Ahasuerus (Xerxes I) of Persia. He is mentioned in the book of Esther as one of those the king sent to bring Queen Vashti to the royal banquet. Although his role is briefly noted, he is part of the important event that led to Esther becoming queen.

keyEvents.title: Service at the king's banquet
keyEvents.description: Karkas was one of the seven courtiers who served at King Ahasuerus's court in Susa. He was present during the great banquet that the king held.

keyEvents.title: Sent to fetch Queen Vashti
keyEvents.description: On the seventh day of the banquet, when the king was merry with wine, he commanded Karkas and the other six courtiers to bring Queen Vashti wearing the royal crown, so that her beauty might be shown to the guests.

keyEvents.title: Queen Vashti's refusal
keyEvents.description: The mission of Karkas and the other courtiers failed when Queen Vashti refused to come at the king's command, leading to a political crisis at the court.

keyEvents.title: Consequences of Vashti's refusal
keyEvents.description: Vashti's refusal, which Karkas witnessed, led to her being deposed as queen, paving the way for Esther to become the new queen and later save the Jewish people.
